stories.title: Nasdaq falls 1.48% as AI stocks give back Monday's surge; Dow ends above 50,000
stories.body: The S&P 500 fell 36.08 points (0.50%) to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq Composite 356.02 points (1.48%) to 23,733.54, while the Dow rose 423.39 points (0.85%) to 50,018.70 and the Russell 2000 gained 0.57% to 2,684.94 (AP, Yahoo Finance). AP said Nvidia and other AI stocks dragged the market back down as Monday's surge faded, though most stocks in the S&P 500 rose; Anthropic sank 6.5% to below its $83 IPO price. The VIX closed at 26.36 (−0.98%).
stories.why: Monday's +4.73% S&P 500 day was partly retraced, with the Dow and Nasdaq moving in opposite directions. Completed 1-hour closes on SPY and QQQ show whether that split carries into Wednesday's data-heavy, pre-holiday session.

stories.title: Apple and Microsoft rise while Amazon, Meta and Alphabet slip
stories.body: Apple closed at $354.07 (+1.43%) and Microsoft at $496.13 (+0.74%), while Amazon ended at $252.29 (−1.21%), Meta at $589.82 (−1.30%) and Alphabet's GOOG at $276.58 (−1.06%), even as the technology sector ETF fell 3.26%. Today's sources gave no company-specific reason for these moves; Yahoo Finance's live blog reported that Microsoft declared an internal 'code red' after a Nov. 12–13 outage that hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot.
stories.why: Megacaps split from chip stocks, holding the S&P 500's loss to half a percent. Their hourly closes relative to Monday's wide ranges show whether money is rotating within tech rather than leaving it.

stories.title: Chip stocks slide: Micron −11%, AMD −9%, Intel −8% as the AI trade comes under renewed pressure
stories.body: Micron closed at $629.79 (−11.01%), AMD at $413.27 (−8.86%), Intel at $54.80 (−8.15%) and Broadcom at $301.08 (−3.98%), giving back part of Monday's rally. Yahoo Finance said chips fell as the overall AI trade came under renewed pressure, and FinanceFeeds put the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down about 9.2% in late-morning trading after a gain of more than 14% Monday. FinanceFeeds also noted a Nov. 23 AMD registration covering the potential resale of about 336.9 million shares, including up to 160 million each tied to warrants held by OpenAI and Meta. Investrade said BNP cut Micron to Neutral with a $775 target, from $1,700.
stories.why: Double-digit swings in both directions on consecutive days keep implied volatility and option premiums in chip names elevated; completed 1-hour closes filter the noise of intrahour reversals.

stories.title: Energy and bank shares help lift the Dow
stories.body: Chevron closed at $208.73 (+1.24%), Exxon at $158.23 (+0.85%), Bank of America at $48.56 (+0.87%) and JPMorgan at $317.10 (+0.14%) as the Dow rose 0.85%; the energy and financial sector ETFs gained 0.97% and 0.83%. January WTI settled at $82.05 (+2.35%) and Brent at $91.40 (+2.27%) (Investrade), rebounding from a three-month low as traders weighed continued ship attacks near the Strait of Hormuz (Rallies).
stories.why: Banks and energy are moving on rates and oil rather than on the AI trade, which shows up as low correlation with QQQ on the hourly chart.

stories.title: Nvidia falls 5.9% a day after its 31% Huang-return surge
stories.body: Nvidia closed at $155.38 (−5.86%) after ending Monday at $165.05 (+31.48%), when the board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. The Motley Fool pointed to profit-taking and to Reuters' report that lawmakers from both parties criticized the rehiring; Reuters also said Huang and the company face FBI, Justice Department and SEC probes and reviews, and The Motley Fool, citing Reuters, reported an SEC probe into Nvidia's accounting practices. Yahoo Finance said the Senate Banking Committee confirmed Huang's testimony will go forward on Dec. 3. After hours the stock was at $152.64 (−1.77%) at 7:01 PM ET (Yahoo Finance).
stories.why: Two sessions with ranges above 9% leave the stock far from its moving averages; with governance and probe headlines still unfolding, completed 1-hour closes matter more than headline prints.

stories.title: Gold and silver slide as Fed-hike bets firm before PCE
stories.body: GLD closed at $325.45 (−2.27%) and SLV at $36.84 (−5.32%). December gold futures settled at $3,561.90 (−2.45%) and December silver at $40.78 (−5.54%) (Investrade). Kitco said a firm dollar and Fed rate-hike expectations — futures priced about 95% odds of a 25 bp hike at the Dec. 8–9 meeting — kept gold from extending Monday's rebound and pressured silver, and Yahoo Finance said a high PCE reading on Wednesday would 'seemingly only cement the Fed's position of raising rates.'
stories.why: Metals ETFs are trading on rate expectations into a scheduled 8:30 AM ET data release, a known overnight gap risk; the next completed hourly candle after the release shows how the market took it.

stories.title: Hormuz ship attacks and a tanker-cyberattack probe keep oil risk in view
stories.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a container ship was targeted near the Strait of Hormuz, and UKMTO said three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles on Monday (Rallies). The Wall Street Journal reported the US is investigating whether Iran was involved in cyberattacks on as many as 50 energy tankers; a Trump administration official said no evidence of Iranian involvement had been found (Cornerstone Futures). January WTI settled at $82.05 (+2.35%) (Investrade); OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday, Nov. 29 (FinanceFeeds). USO closed at $135.43 (+1.55%) and Occidental at $53.38 (+1.29%).
stories.why: Headline-driven oil can gap between sessions, and the Thanksgiving break adds a day without US trading; USO and OXY hourly closes show whether the market prices the incidents as supply risk.

stories.title: VIX closes at 26.36 as stocks split
stories.body: The VIX ended Tuesday at 26.36 (−0.98%) (Yahoo Finance), after a late-morning reading of 28.87 (FinanceFeeds); it closed Monday at 26.62. Saxo's Tuesday options brief said Monday's rally flattened the volatility curve: all six VIX tenors sat between 25.47 and 27.76, the VIX3M/VIX ratio rose to 0.96 and the SKEW index was 140.37.
stories.why: A VIX in the mid-20s keeps option premiums and expected moves well above normal, and a flat curve means near-dated protection is priced about the same as longer-dated.

stories.title: 5-year auction tails slightly as December hike odds hold near 95%
stories.body: The Treasury sold $70 billion of 5-year notes at a 4.719% high yield, a 0.3 bp tail to the 4.716% when-issued level, with a 2.37 bid-to-cover (investingLive); TheStreet Pro called it the thirteenth straight tail. The 10-year yield ended at 4.904%, down 1.4 bp (Yahoo Finance, Investrade). Yahoo Finance said traders priced a 95% chance of a 25 bp Fed hike in December and 5% odds of 50 bp. A $44 billion 7-year sale follows Wednesday at 11:30 AM ET (KCEX).
stories.why: Rate-hike pricing is the macro backdrop for the tech pullback; auction results and Wednesday's PCE can move yields and index ETFs within a single hourly candle.

stories.title: Asia rallies on Huang's return while Europe slips on chip and tariff worries
stories.body: Trading Economics reported Japan's Nikkei 225 up 3.91% to 58,645 in a post-holiday session and Korea's KOSPI up 6.32% to 5,006.03 on renewed AI optimism after Huang's reinstatement, while the Shanghai Composite rose 0.27% to 3,548.37; 24/7 Wall St. said the Hang Seng closed down 0.82%. In Europe the DAX fell 1.29% to 25,012 as Infineon and Siemens Energy led losses amid reports of new US tariff pushes, the FTSE 100 slipped 0.13% to 10,467 as miners led declines, and the CAC 40 edged up 0.2% to 8,057, helped by Sanofi's $41 billion Insmed deal.
stories.why: Overseas chip suppliers moved with Monday's US rally before Tuesday's US pullback, so overnight markets are lagging the US tape this week.

stories.title: Consumer confidence jumps to 103.3 in November
stories.body: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 in November from 91.9 in October, against a consensus of about 92 (92.2 per TheStreet Pro, 92.5 per The Rio Times). The Present Situation Index rose to 132.8 and the Expectations Index to 83.6. The Rio Times reported that respondents saying jobs are 'plentiful' rose to 30.8% from 26.2%, and 12-month inflation expectations were 5.7%.
stories.why: A strong data surprise adds to the case the Fed is already pricing for a December hike; Wednesday's PCE release is the next scheduled data risk.

stories.title: Options price about a 2% S&P 500 move into Friday; chip implied volatility stays high
stories.body: Saxo's Tuesday options brief said S&P 500 options priced about 151.80 points (2.09%) of movement into the Nov. 27 expiry, down from 271.80 in its prior edition. At Monday's close, implied-volatility rank was 75.5 for Nvidia and 77.0 for the semiconductor fund, against a median single-name rank of 39.2. Longbridge counted 11,004,818 Nvidia options traded Monday, 60% of them calls.
stories.why: Expected-move pricing shows how wide a range the options market allows through the holiday-shortened week; it is reported market data, not a signal.

stories.title: Ahead: PCE, GDP and claims at 8:30 AM Wednesday, then Thanksgiving
stories.body: Wednesday at 8:30 AM ET brings October personal income and outlays with the PCE price index (core forecast +0.3% m/m, the same as the prior month), the second estimate of Q3 GDP (forecast 3.5% vs 3.4% initially) and weekly jobless claims (forecast 201,000), per Gotrade, plus October durable goods. The Treasury sells $44 billion of 7-year notes at 11:30 AM ET (KCEX) and the Fed's Beige Book is due at 2:00 PM ET. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close at 1:00 PM ET Friday. OPEC+ meets Nov. 29, Huang's Senate Banking testimony is set for Dec. 3, the Fed meets Dec. 8–9, and Broadcom reports Dec. 9 after the close.
stories.why: A heavy data morning before a holiday break means fewer completed hourly candles and possible gaps around Thursday's closure and Friday's early close.
